newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 10.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Tuesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Philippine shares are likely to trade in a narrow band between the 2,850 to 2,600 range as both foreign and local investors remain sceptical of the market's rise on Monday since it was accompanied by extremely light volume, said BPI Securities Corp analyst Roberto Cano.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities expects the market will not be able to sustain its climb as investors would cash-in gains.
* On Monday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended 15.57 points higher at 2,778.37.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 42.72 points higher at 7,478.50. PLDT's ADR dropped $0 3/8 to $59 1/8.
* The Philippine peso closed higher at 26.379 to the dollar vs 26.390.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 14.03125 percent.
* The Philippines will ask for a four-month extension of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme which is due to expire on June 23, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said.
* International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) said it is looking at investing in more foreign ports after its two existing ones proved to be profitable.
* ICTSI also said traffic volume in its Manila port had picked up in April and May after a slow start in the first quarter of the year.
* Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc said its board of directors has approved a buyback of shares which were undervalued.

* Bayan Telecommunications Holding Corp (BayanTel), the telecoms arm of Benpres Holdings Corp urged the government to award underserved areas to deserving carriers and to settle interconnection disputes between various firms.
* Reynolds Philippines Corp, one of the country's biggest manufacturers of aluminum products, said a tariff cut on imported aluminum was hurting its business.
* Cebu Property Ventures & Development Corp said it posted a net income of 43.7 million pesos for the first quarter of 1997, up 491 percent from 7.4 million pesos in the year-ago period.
* The Central Bank said it was not trying to push down the peso despite last Friday's hike in its dollar rate, CB Treasurer Sergio Edeza said.
* The yield on the Philippine 91-day treasury bill fell to 10.293 percent on Monday from 10.529 a week ago, the Bureau of Treasury said.
* The Central Bank said it was raising the interest rate on loans to exporters by 0.25 percentage points to an annual 5.6875 percent, with immediate effect.
* Ayala Bain Insurance Brokers Inc, a unit of Ayala Corp, said it had agreed to merge with CityTrust Insurance Brokers Corp (CIBC).

* Victorias Milling Corp denied reports in Philippine newspapers of alleged loan irregularities involving 500 million pesos. An official said Victorias' bank loans were covered by mortgage indenture s and sugar quedans (warehouses).
* A. Soriano Corp said it had abandoned a cement joint venture project with Global Equities Inc and some Japanese firms.

* Newspaper Philippine Star said that ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp is expanding its reach in the local film industry with the setting up of RoadRunner Network Inc, a post-production outfit that will provide state-of-the-art digital technology for movies and television.

* The Manila Times said the Ayala and Lopez groups who won the bid for the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System has moved their takeover of operations from July to August to allow external auditors to sort out the water utility's billing system.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer said President Fidel Ramos will step down in 1998 even if the Supreme Court decided to allow a group, the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action (Pirma) to campaign for a plebiscite on lifting term limits on elective officials.
